how: Members proposed and began distinct fan images that others were invited to join.
Calls recruited members to build emblems and characters.
A representation call received a bare report of joining the work.
A bare joining reply answers the representation call without explaining acceptance.
Starting and recruitment can occupy the same proposal rather than forming separate chronological stages.
The representation thread contains the call followed by reports of completed work.
Written uptake and completion reports cannot establish how much construction the call caused or how silent placers joined.
Participants judged particular designs and threatened works beyond their available hands.
Participants proposed, enlarged and revised multiple emblems and characters.
Members reported completed parts, borders and the whale.
Members circulated coordinates and templates to align contributions.
Published templates supplied provisional targets while design argument and revision continued.
Organizers carried privately developed plans back to public placers who lacked chat access.

statement: Screening planning access and carrying decisions back to public placers
how: Private planning required screened entry and public summaries so participants outside the chat could coordinate their pixels.

why: A single room cannot test the model's aggregate frequency claim about decided organization.
The record documents a prank mirror bot and human coordination but does not establish scripts or spare accounts placing pixels.
Upkeep pressure is visible but no passage establishes a resulting turn to machine placement.

how: Participants guarded, repaired and restored vulnerable works while prioritizing defense.
A completion announcement explicitly asks continued effort because the work could be swept away.
Building and upkeep overlap rather than succeeding each other as exclusive stages.
Participants distinguished intentional cracks, mistaken restoration and encroachment disowned as splinter activity.
Participants negotiated pixel shifts, borders and promises to stop mutual griefing.
Visitors carried proposals and repair assurances on behalf of neighboring groups.
Reports of territorial fighting were answered with negotiated shifts intended to preserve the work.
Participants invoked truces, apologized and asked their own placers to spare neighboring work.
A settled border was explicitly invoked to prevent expansion and repair a neighbor's text.
Restraint required agreements to reach placers who understood the intended design and were willing to comply.
Treaty reports coexisted with claims that trolls could not be controlled and explicit rejection of peace.
Uninformed placement and misunderstanding must be distinguished from knowing rejection of an agreement.
A reported diplomatic move prompted explicit personal refusal of peace despite the intergroup agreement.
Participants traded repair promises and offered whale protection in exchange for help defending a goose.
A threatened whale drew an offer of protection exchanged for future defensive help.
An apology about territorial interference received an answering promise to repair the neighboring flag.
Defenders called on allied communities and reported support through their shared chats.
Reported support from existing allies does not establish that this threat caused coalition formation.
A permitted personal mark was moved within negotiated territory while further reimplementation remained conditional.
Host permission remained subject to subsequent negotiations among neighboring groups rather than securing permanent control.
Repositioning included accommodating friendly art and negotiating a gem move rather than only abandoning a defeated location.
Capacity problems permitted giving up, holding survivors or attempting restoration, not necessarily relocation.
Participants carried fan lore into design choices and moral arguments about relations with neighbors.

statement: Using fan lore to judge competing ways of acting
how: Inherited fiction supplied competing standards for restraint and retaliation rather than merely identifying a rival.
Participants used the protagonist's example to justify returning space and reproach retaliatory anger.

why: The coded territorial grievances do not establish a pre-canvas quarrel between the communities.
Lore informs conduct but the cited attack turns do not establish a prior tie naming the rival in that turn.

how: The subreddit staged a Lapis takeover that members extended through jokes and requests to retain the appearance.
Participants carried the takeover joke into a recurring collaborative drawing session.
Moderators gathered canvas posts into a megathread and redirected a separate repair post there.
A moderator explicitly attributed the megathread to canvas posts clogging the subreddit.
Members announced finished work, thanked helpers and later credited collaborative construction.
Reports of completed images were accompanied by celebration and thanks.
Participants recorded histories and timelapses and mourned losses while recognizing survivors.
Celebration and documentation occur in the record without establishing that celebration caused the recording effort.
After closure participants hoped for a cleaned image and corrected accounts of neighboring groups' conduct.
A cleanup hope and account corrections do not demonstrate an implemented shared-copy cleanup or a dispute over preserving scars.
Members proposed preserving Peridot in an atlas and restarting pixel work through clone links.
Proposed preservation and restart are visible without evidence of collective uptake or a durable successor group.
Documentation and continuation proposals do not establish that a record caused a new collective effort.
Participants called for replacing another mark and retaliating against territorial encroachment.
Build calls and later attack calls share the room but do not identify which recruited placers turned to attack.
A proposal to convert another group's mark received a reasoned refusal to destroy others' work.
Attack proposals received counterproposals invoking cooperation or denying the claimed declaration of war.
Participants continued the territorial contest through blame and vows never to forget after closure.
Postclosure blame follows attack calls but does not independently establish every attacker's identity or motive.
